# FOSSCast

Self-hosted podcast hosting. Free software under the GNU AGPL v3, written
by Lightmorphic Ltd (company number 17423646, England and Wales).
Source: https://github.com/lightmorphic/fosscast

## Where it stands

Version 0.1.0, a public beta. It is not ready to be relied on: data loss
and breaking changes are possible, and nobody should put a real podcast on
it yet. Releases are marked as pre-release on GitHub.

## What it is

A podcast platform you run on your own server. One pasted docker-compose
file installs it. It gives a podcast a website with a page per episode and
a page per host, an RSS feed carrying the full iTunes namespace and the
modern Podcasting 2.0 tags, and download statistics drawn on your own
server from counters that cannot be joined back to a person.

## How to install it

Paste the file at https://fosscast.org/#install into docker-compose.yml
and run `docker compose up -d`. There is nothing in the file to fill in:
FOSSCast prints a setup code in its log, and the first person to open
the site gives it that code and chooses their own login, with a passkey
and a second factor offered at the same time. The image is
ghcr.io/lightmorphic/fosscast:latest. The bundled Caddy is optional:
nginx, Apache, a Cloudflare Tunnel and a Tailscale-only instance are all
supported.

## What it deliberately does not do

- It never phones home. No update check, no telemetry, no crash
  reporting, no CDN, no third-party font or script.
- It sets no cookie for listeners and builds no listener profile.
- It does not require you to store audio on the same machine: an
  episode can point at a file anywhere that serves byte ranges.

## Cost

Nothing, forever, on your own machine. There is no paid tier of the
software and no feature held behind a subscription.

## Related

Castmorphic (https://castmorphic.com) is a paid service that runs
FOSSCast for you and adds hosted-only extras. The software here is the
same software; the service around it is the product.
